description: At its heart floats a knot of contained antimatter barely a kilometer wide, wrapped in shells of negated vacuum that swell outward like blooming petals. Annihilation flashes flare along its skin without warning, bright enough to blind unfiltered optics. Long-range sensors register positron signatures across twenty-two million kilometers.

The Reliquary pulses on no fixed schedule, its containment layers budding new chambers and collapsing old ones. Anything solid that crosses its boundary annihilates in a silent white flash. Even hardened probes survive minutes at most before erasure.

The survey ship Kestrel's Lantern was lost mapping the anomaly; her final transmission was a burst of gamma static and one word, 'budding.' Later probes confirmed the pocket neither grows nor fades, contradicting every model of antimatter storage. Its persistence suggests engineering, but nothing about it shows intent.

The site is interdicted by treaty, though its flashes still lure theorists who insist the containment is a mechanism waiting to be understood. Whoever built it, if anyone did, left no other trace. Approach within five million kilometers and you become part of its record.
